title: Arm-B-bound full-enwik9 decode from an enumerated minimal runtime root

supersedes.reason: stale archive identity and broad host base visibility

activation_dependencies: Arm B terminal archive identity frozen
Arm B exact raw inverse passed
scratch has at least the preregistered free-space margin

phases.method: Trace the terminal Arm B archive under a broad read-only base to enumerate execve, open/openat, stat-family, access, readlink, mmap-backed objects, environment reads, and network syscalls for every descendant.

Copy only the submission archive and exact discovered base files into a new content-addressed root. Replace loader symlinks with bound regular files or prove every link target remains inside the root.

Read-only bind the minimal root as sandbox /, add only declared writable work/output/tmp mounts and kernel interfaces, clear the environment, unshare all namespaces, and execute the archive with no input.
phases.canonical_comparison: Compare the output to canonical enwik9 outside the sandbox after execution; canonical enwik9 is never visible to the decoder.

phases.method: Normalize the sealed replay trace and require every successful read to resolve to a root-manifest file, an archive-extracted child, a declared writable artifact, or an allowed kernel interface. Require no network syscall attempts.
Recreate the root and scratch from retained manifests and repeat the complete decode. Require output, process closure, file-access closure, and resource-boundary identity.

process_closure.extracted_child_requirement: Bind each child executable hash to an offset/length or deterministic extraction hash from the terminal archive.
process_closure.dynamic_object_requirement: Every loaded object must be present in the root manifest with exact path, bytes, SHA-256, provider class, and counted status.

successful_read_allowlist: runtime-generated file under declared writable mount

terminal_gates: archive identity equals terminal Arm B
all executed images declared or archive-derived

official_boundary.reason: The official rules allow standard file-I/O libraries but do not define the exact permitted base-system closure. This receipt proves Gamma's enumerated dependency boundary; committee interpretation remains separate.
forbidden_claims: A dependency-sealed decode proves compressor eligibility.
A dependency-sealed decode proves official memory or runtime eligibility.
The 1MB broad-base preflight proves this full-corpus closure.
